packages.name: Steam
packages.summary: Discover, authenticate, and launch games from a local Steam installation.
packages.description: Reads your local Steam installation and authenticated Steam library through unu's provider sandbox. Launch, install, and uninstall actions are still described by the provider and executed by the core.

packages.name: SteamGridDB
packages.summary: Fetch richer cover, background, and logo art from SteamGridDB.
packages.description: Uses your SteamGridDB API key to enrich discovered games with cover, background, and logo art. The provider returns asset references; unu resolves and caches the images.

packages.name: IGDB
packages.summary: Fetch descriptions, genres, release info, screenshots, and video trailers from IGDB.
packages.description: Uses a Twitch app-access token to enrich discovered games with descriptions, genres, developers, release years, ratings, cover/background art, screenshots, and video trailers for the game detail view. The provider returns asset references and video descriptors; unu resolves, caches, and serves the images.

packages.name: Epic Games Store
packages.summary: Discover, authenticate, and launch games from Epic Games Store.
packages.description: Reads local Epic Games Launcher manifests for installed games and overlays the authenticated owned library through Epic services. Launch, install, and uninstall actions are descriptions returned to the core launch choke point.

packages.name: Microsoft Store
packages.summary: Discover locally installed Xbox and Microsoft Store games.
packages.description: Experimental local discovery from a user-configured Xbox app install root. Package identity, never folder or title similarity, is used for deduplication. Microsoft exposes no supported third-party ownership API, so this reports installed packages only.

packages.name: Xbox Game Pass
packages.summary: Show your Xbox Game Pass catalog and hand off install/launch to the Microsoft Store.
packages.description: Reads the public PC Game Pass catalog without signing in. PackageIdentityName provides a hard join to Microsoft Store installs when present; Win32 titles without it remain catalog-only. Install and Launch describe Microsoft Store product-page handoffs.

packages.name: Ubisoft+
packages.summary: Show the live Ubisoft+ PC catalog and hand off install/launch to Ubisoft Connect.
packages.description: Shows the live Ubisoft+ PC catalog without asserting account ownership. Install, Launch, and Uninstall describe handoffs to Ubisoft Connect; local install detection belongs to the separate Ubisoft Connect provider.

packages.name: Ubisoft Connect
packages.summary: Discover configured Ubisoft Connect installs and launch them through Ubisoft Connect.
packages.description: Experimental local Ubisoft discovery. Because the current registry port cannot enumerate install subkeys, product ids must be configured explicitly; the provider then verifies each id against Ubisoft Connect's install registry and never guesses by title.

packages.name: Soft
packages.summary: Warm, restrained focus and activation sounds for couch navigation.
packages.description: An original two-cue sound pack with short PCM WAV feedback for focus movement and activation.

packages.name: Deck
packages.summary: A dense couch dashboard with hero art, shelves, and gamepad-first controls.
packages.description: Deck uses large media, compact metadata, and quick library filters for a console-style launcher surface.

packages.name: Grey (reference)
packages.summary: A quiet reference layout with compact cards and restrained contrast.
packages.description: Grey is a minimal system-style theme for validating layout, focus, and settings surfaces without decorative treatment.

packages.name: GameStation
packages.summary: A PS5-inspired theme where the selected game's art becomes the room and the chrome is colourless glass.
packages.description: GameStation dissolves into the cover art: the game you point at fills the whole screen, the chrome is neutral glass that gets out of the way, and a square app-tile row floats up top. Calm, immersive, smooth — every bit of colour comes from the art, never the shell.

packages.name: XSquare
packages.summary: An Xbox-inspired system dashboard: one decisive green, squared chrome, and a fast horizontal blade strip.
packages.description: XSquare sits on top of your cover art like an operating system — squared geometry, a single confident green for focus and active states, wide landscape blade tiles in a horizontal strip, and a dense, left-anchored readout. Motion snaps rather than glides. It renders only real game data.

packages.name: NexusDeck
packages.summary: A Heroic-inspired TV dashboard with a vertical system rail, poster wall library, and full-bleed game detail art.
packages.description: NexusDeck blends the reference screens into a couch launcher: a dim left rail, centered poster grid, vivid magenta focus, glassy footer chrome, and cinematic detail pages where real game art carries the scene.
